subject.title: feat(hooks): add waitForResult mode to POST /hooks/agent endpoint

question: Should OpenClaw accept `waitForResult` and `announceToMain` on the existing `POST /hooks/agent` endpoint with synchronous raw result/error responses, or require a different result-return contract before merge?
rationale: This changes a public authenticated gateway hook boundary and decides output disclosure, error disclosure, replay, timeout, and session-observation semantics that automation cannot safely choose.

options.title: Approve current endpoint shape with guardrails
options.body: Accept the existing `waitForResult`/`announceToMain` direction after the mapped replay response and latest-head proof gaps are closed and output/error bounds are explicitly owned.

options.title: Request a different sync contract
options.body: Ask the contributor to reshape the feature around a dedicated sync endpoint, result token, or fetch-after-run flow if that better fits the security boundary.

options.title: Decline core sync hooks
options.body: Keep `/hooks/agent` async-only and route synchronous orchestration to downstream plugins or caller-managed polling if maintainers do not want this surface in core.

recommendation.title: Approve current endpoint shape with guardrails
recommendation.body: Accept the existing `waitForResult`/`announceToMain` direction after the mapped replay response and latest-head proof gaps are closed and output/error bounds are explicitly owned.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest sampled gateway API and hook session-routing history, and this decision is broader than a narrow code defect.
